Sofia  thanks for the great questions. Quick answers inline, and looping in Marissa for the technical detail and lead times.

> 1) When you say Hosted API (EU region)  does that mean all customer request and data (including logs and KV cache) are kept in the EU region and never routed outside for processing?

Short answer: Yes for standard Hosted in the EU region  request processing and persistent storage (logs, audit, model artifacts) remain in-region. There are a few edge cases (e.g., fallback to a compatible model in another region if capacity is exhausted) which we can control with routing policies and explicit contractual commitments. Marissa  can you confirm the default guarantees we can include in an SOC2/contract clause?

> 2) If we start with Hosted for speed of onboarding and later move to Dedicated or Private, how smooth is the migration? Any expected downtime or compatibility concerns (model versions, quantization differences)?

We support pinned model versions and containerized model artifacts to make migrations low-friction. Typical migrations (Hosted -> Dedicated) are designed to be near-seamless with a short cutover window; detailed runbook will help minimize downtime. Private (VPC/on-prem) can take longer (infrastructure setup, network peering, KMS integration)  Marissa will include ballpark timelines.

> 3) For APAC users, would cross-region routing to an APAC host be required? If so, is that per-request routing or can we limit APAC traffic to non-PII flows only?

Routing is policy-driven and can be per-route or per-customer. You can configure routes such that PII flows remain EU-only and non-PII/low-risk traffic can be routed to APAC for latency reasons. Well include an example routing policy in the doc.

Marissa / Aditya  can you add: lead times (Dedicated vs Private), expected pricing delta ballpark, and a simple migration checklist? Also attaching the Deployment Options doc I referenced earlier.

Thanks 
Dylan

Hi Sofia / Oliver  thanks for the detailed questions. Attaching a concise tech note (Redwood_Deployment_Options.pdf) and pasted a short summary below. Happy to run a 3045 minute technical deep-dive with your infra/security folks  Im available Tue/Thu mornings PST next week.

Summary (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)  focused on data residency & routing:

1) Hosted (EU region)
- Data residency: Persistent storage (logs, audit trails, model artifacts) and request processing are kept in the EU region. We offer contractual EU-only processing guarantees for Hosted (we can add explicit routing/capacity fallbacks exceptions to the contract).
- Cross-region routing: By default we keep traffic in-region; policy-based fallbacks are available (e.g., when EU capacity is saturated we can fail-open or route to a compatible model in another region  configurable).
- Lead time: Fastest (hours to days).
- Use-case fit: Rapid POC and production for EU-only workloads with standard compliance needs.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity in EU)
- Data residency: Full EU residency, no shared compute with other tenants.
- SLA: Higher uptime and latency guarantees; tail latency improvements for steady-throughput workloads.
- Lead time: ~26 weeks depending on capacity and region availability.
- Use-case fit: Predictable throughput, tighter SLA, and data isolation for regulated workloads.

3) Private (VPC or on-prem)
- Data residency: Entire control plane is customer-managed; customer can require all traffic never leaves on-prem/VPC. KMS/HSM integrations available for key sovereignty.
- Lead time: 612+ weeks (networking, security review, peering & KMS).
- Use-case fit: Highest compliance/regulatory needs (no shared control plane).

Routing & policy recommendations:
- Recommend a two-tier routing policy: PII routes tagged -> enforce EU-only and never-route-out; Non-PII routes -> prefer EU, fallback to APAC for latency.
- Implement request-level tagging at your app boundary so Redwood routing can enforce per-request behavior.

Migration notes:
- Hosted -> Dedicated: low friction. We support pinning model versions and exporting KV cache snapshots for cutover. Planned short maintenance window recommended.
- Hosted -> Private: additional ops work (network peering, KMS), expect longer lead time and a security review.

Ballpark pricing & lead times (very rough):
- Hosted (EU): pay-as-you-go, fastest onboarding.
- Dedicated (EU): commitment-based, ~1.31.8x hosted unit cost depending on commit and capacity.
- Private: licensing + infra + services, 23x hosted unit cost once amortized (depends on infra).
